# Identifying Environmentally Responsible US Public Transit Systems

Green Transit Alliance (GTA) will be looking into the  “greenest” public transit agencies. Each year, GTA awards prizes to the small, medium, and large transit agencies that score the highest on the GTA Value Index (GTA VI). The GTA VI estimates the effective emissions reductions achieved by each agency, using a combination of:

- Local ridership data (both number and distance); and
- Emissions estimates of public transit vehicles (either direct tailpipe emissions or upstream emissions from electrical generation)


By comparing these to the tailpipe emissions that would have occured if all riders had instead driven to their destination, the VI identifies the most valuable public transit agencies in the country.



### Data Acquisition

#### State Electricity Profiles

For this project, lets assume that all electricity generation in a state is fungible, we will assign the average generation emissions to all electric transit in a state, even if the transit authority officially has a “green supply” agreement in place.


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(fs)

has_table <- function(path){
  if(!file_exists(path) || file_size(path) == 0) return(FALSE)
  tryCatch(
    !inherits(read_html(path) |> html_element("table"), "xml_missing"),
    error = function(e) FALSE
  )
}

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
  state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")

  dir_name  <- path("data", "mp02")
  file_name <- path(dir_name, state_formatted)
  dir_create(dir_name, recurse = TRUE)

  if(!has_table(file_name)){
    if(file_exists(file_name)) file_delete(file_name)   # clear bad cache

    request("https://www.eia.gov") |>
      req_url_path("electricity", "state", state_formatted) |>
      req_headers(`User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |>
      req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
      req_throttle(rate = 1) |>              # be polite, avoid being blocked
      req_perform(path = file_name) |>
      resp_check_status()

    if(!has_table(file_name)){
      file_delete(file_name)
      stop("No table found on EIA page for: ", state)
    }
  }

  TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |>
    html_element("table") |>
    html_table() |>
    mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))

  if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
    TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
  }

  get_val <- function(item){
    TABLE |> filter(Item == item) |> pull(Value) |>
      str_replace_all(",", "") |> as.numeric()
  }

  data.frame(
    CO2_MWh                = get_val("carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)"),
    primary_source         = TABLE |> filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> pull(Rank),
    electricity_price_MWh  = get_val("average retail price (cents/kwh)") * 10, # cents/kWh -> $/MWh
    generation_MWh         = get_val("net generation (megawatthours)"),
    state                  = state,
    abbreviation           = abbr
  )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()


```

Lets look at the report in a table form to make it easier to get a holistic view of the data that we will be analyzing in this project. 

```{r}
library(gt)

# transforming the data into a table form

EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(generation_MWh)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(State = paste0(state, " (", abbreviation, ")")) |>
  select(CO2_MWh, primary_source, electricity_price_MWh, generation_MWh, State) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    CO2_MWh               = "Pounds of CO2 Emitted Per MWh of Electricity Produced",
    primary_source        = "Primary Source of Electricity Generation",
    electricity_price_MWh = "Average Retail Price for 1000 kWh",
    generation_MWh        = "Total Generation Capacity (MWh)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(CO2_MWh, generation_MWh), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_currency(columns = electricity_price_MWh, currency = "USD", decimals = 2) |>
  cols_align(align = "right", columns = c(CO2_MWh, electricity_price_MWh, generation_MWh)) |>
  cols_align(align = "left",  columns = c(primary_source, State)) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100),
    column_labels.font.weight = "normal"
  )

```

Here, we have collected the effective emissions per MWh[^mwh] as well as price and total state-wide generation capacity. We will use this data to compare the emissions of different transit modalities.


#### Energy Consumption

Turning to the National Transit Database to get information on various public transit authorities.

```{r}
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()

```


#### Transit Service Provided

Finally, we want the 2025 Service by Agency report, from which we will extract characteristics of typical passenger trips on each transit service.

```{r}

load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()

```

#### Recoding the Mode column

The Mode column holds two-letter NTD codes like “HR” and “MB,” so we need to recode them into callable names like Heavy Rail or Bus to make the tables and results interpret-able and to keep modes consistent across the energy and service data sets.

```{r}

NTD_ENERGY  |> distinct(Mode) |> arrange(Mode)
NTD_SERVICE |> distinct(mode) |> arrange(mode)

recode_mode <- function(x){
  recode_values(x,
    "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
    "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
    "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
    "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
    "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
    "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
    "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
    "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
    "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
    "MB" ~ "Bus",
    "MG" ~ "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
    "PB" ~ "Publico",
    "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
    "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
    "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
    "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
    "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
    "YR" ~ "Hybrid Rail",
    default = "Unknown")
}

NTD_ENERGY  <- NTD_ENERGY  |> mutate(Mode = recode_mode(Mode))
NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |> mutate(mode = recode_mode(mode))

```

Lets check to confirm that it worked.

```{r}

NTD_ENERGY  |> count(Mode, sort = TRUE)
NTD_SERVICE |> count(mode, sort = TRUE)

```

#### EDA - EIA State Electricity Profiles

**Which 5 states have the most expensive retail electricity? (Graph)**

```{r}

library(gganimate)
top5_price <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)

grow <- crossing(top5_price, frame = 0:30) |>
  mutate(shown = electricity_price_MWh * frame / 30)

p2 <- ggplot(grow, aes(x = shown, y = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#31BAE9") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::dollar(shown, accuracy = 0.1)),
            hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar,
                     limits = c(0, max(top5_price$electricity_price_MWh) * 1.15)) +
  labs(title = "Top 5 States by Average Retail Electricity Price",
       x = "Average retail price ($ per MWh)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  transition_manual(frame)

animate(p2, nframes = 31, fps = 10, end_pause = 15)

top_state    <- top5_price$state[1]
top_price    <- round(top5_price$electricity_price_MWh[1], 2)
other_states <- paste(top5_price$state[2:5], collapse = ", ")

```
`r top_state` has the most expensive retail electricity at $`r top_price` per MWh. The other four are `r other_states`.

#### EDA - NTD Energy Usage

**What is the least commonly used fuel source for US public transit? (Inline)**

```{r}

# reshape energy columns to get totals by fuel type
fuel_totals <- NTD_ENERGY %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with(c("Gallons", "Kilowatt", "Kilograms")), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(), 
    names_to = "fuel", 
    values_to = "total"
  ) %>%
  mutate(fuel = str_remove_all(fuel, "Gallons of |Kilowatt hours of |Kilograms of "))

# unused fuels (total == 0)
least_fuel <- fuel_totals %>%
  filter(total == 0) %>%
  pull(fuel) %>%
  knitr::combine_words()

# least used fuel among active fuels (total > 0)
least_used_info <- fuel_totals %>%
  filter(total > 0) %>%
  slice_min(total, n = 1)

least_used_fuel <- knitr::combine_words(least_used_info$fuel)
least_used_gal  <- format(round(least_used_info$total), big.mark = ",")


```

It seems like no agency reported using `r least_fuel`. Among fuels that were used, the least common is `r least_used_fuel`, with `r least_used_gal` gallons across all agencies.

### Data Analysis


#### Calculate Total Emissions

Lets build a table that join the three tables (NTD_SERVICE, NTD_ENERGY, and EIA_SEP_REPORT) together and computes the total emissions associated with each Agency + Mode pair.


```{r}


service_lookup <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  distinct(NTD_ID, mode, state)

# does each agency + mode have only one state? 
service_lookup |>
  count(NTD_ID, mode) |>
  filter(n > 1)


# connect state (NTD_SERVICE) to the fuel columns (NTD_ENERGY) using agency ID and mode
# 
# 
energy_ids <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = str_pad(`NTD ID`, width = 5, pad = "0"))

emissions_table <- left_join(energy_ids,
                             service_lookup,
                             join_by(NTD_ID == NTD_ID, Mode == mode))

# using left join again bc i want to keep every row of emissions_table and look up the state’s CO2 value
# 
eia_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh)

emissions_table <- left_join(emissions_table,
                             eia_co2,
                             join_by(state == abbreviation))
# glimpse of the table
nrow(emissions_table)                 
sum(is.na(emissions_table$state))      
sum(is.na(emissions_table$CO2_MWh))    
glimpse(emissions_table)



# calculating total emissions in pounds of CO2

emissions_table <- emissions_table |>
  mutate(
    # total electricity used, in kWh
    electricity_kwh = `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
                      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`,

    # electricity emissions: 0 if no electricity is used, otherwise kWh / 1000 * state lbs per MWh
    electricity_lbs = if_else(electricity_kwh == 0,
                              0,
                              electricity_kwh / 1000 * CO2_MWh),

    # total emissions = fuels + electricity
    total_emissions_lbs =
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`              * 22.47 +
      `Gallons of Gasoline`                 * 17.86 +   # check this factor against your source
      `Gallons of Kerosene`                 * 21.78 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`  * 12.68 +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`              * 24.78 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`        * 9.83 +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`   * 13.34 +   # check this factor too
      electricity_lbs
  )

# display the first 10 rows in a table
emissions_table |>
  select(`Agency Name`, Mode, state, CO2_MWh,
         `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, `Gallons of Gasoline`,
         `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`,
         `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`, `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`,
         `Gallons of Ethanol`, `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`, `Gallons of Kerosene`,
         `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`, `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`,
         `Kilograms of Hydrogen`, total_emissions_lbs) |>
  head(10) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(`Agency Name` = md("**Agency**"),
             Mode          = md("**Mode**"),
             state         = md("**State**"),
             CO2_MWh       = md("**CO2 (lbs per MWh)**"),
             `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`                = "Diesel",
             `Gallons of Gasoline`                   = "Gasoline",
             `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`     = "CNG",
             `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`                 = "Bio-Diesel",
             `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`    = "LPG",
             `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`          = "LNG",
             `Gallons of Ethanol`                    = "Ethanol",
             `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`                = "Bunker",
             `Gallons of Kerosene`                   = "Kerosene",
             `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`    = "Battery",
             `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` = "Propulsion",
             `Kilograms of Hydrogen`                 = "Hydrogen",
             total_emissions_lbs = md("**Total CO2 (lbs)**")) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Gallons", columns = 5:13) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Kilowatt hours", columns = 14:15) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Kilograms", columns = 16) |>
  tab_header(title    = "Total Emissions by Agency and Mode",
             subtitle = "First 10 Agency + Mode pairs") |>
  tab_source_note(md("Data from the FTA National Transit Database (NTD) and the EIA State Electricity Profiles and CO2 emissions coefficients.")) |>
  fmt_number(columns = 4:17, decimals = 0) |>
  sub_missing(columns = everything(), missing_text = "NA") |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = 1:3) |>
  opt_row_striping()

```


#### Relate Total Emissions and Passenger Service

**Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage**

```{r}
# 1. Summarize total emissions at the Agency level
agency_emissions <- emissions_table |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    total_emissions_lbs = sum(total_emissions_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Summarize usage metrics using exact column names from NTD_SERVICE
agency_usage <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_pmt = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Join emissions with usage and compute normalized metrics
normalized_emissions <- agency_emissions |>
  left_join(agency_usage, by = "NTD_ID") |>
  filter(total_upt > 0, total_pmt > 0, total_emissions_lbs > 0) |>
  mutate(
    emissions_per_upt = total_emissions_lbs / total_upt,
    emissions_per_pmt = total_emissions_lbs / total_pmt,
    agency_size = case_when(
      total_upt >= 10000000 ~ "Large (>= 10M UPT)",
      total_upt >= 1000000  ~ "Medium (1M - 10M UPT)",
      TRUE                  ~ "Small (< 1M UPT)"
    )
  )

# 4. Top 3 most efficient agencies per size tier (by PMT)
most_efficient_by_pmt <- normalized_emissions |>
  group_by(agency_size) |>
  slice_min(order_by = emissions_per_pmt, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  arrange(agency_size, emissions_per_pmt)

# 5. Format GT output table
most_efficient_by_pmt |>
  select(`Agency Name`, agency_size, total_emissions_lbs, total_upt, total_pmt, emissions_per_upt, emissions_per_pmt) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "agency_size") |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name`       = md("**Agency**"),
    total_emissions_lbs = md("**Total CO2 (lbs)**"),
    total_upt           = md("**Total UPT**"),
    total_pmt           = md("**Total PMT**"),
    emissions_per_upt   = md("**lbs CO2 / UPT**"),
    emissions_per_pmt   = md("**lbs CO2 / PMT**")
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Most Efficient Transit Agencies by CO2 Emissions",
    subtitle = "Top agencies per size tier normalized by Passenger Miles Traveled (PMT)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(total_emissions_lbs, total_upt, total_pmt),
    decimals = 0
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(emissions_per_upt, emissions_per_pmt),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping()

```

Looking at the table, from the large agencies, Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) leads with 0.020 lbs CO2/PMT. WMATA benefits heavily from high-capacity heavy rail (Metrorail) powered by regional electrical grid efficiencies and long passenger trip lengths. On the other hand, from the medium agency, City of Seattle leads with 0.064 lbs CO2/PMT. Lastly, from the small agencies, Muncie Indiana Transit System leads with 0.128 lbs CO2/PMT.

## GTA IV IS FINALLY OUT
### Green Transit Alliance (GTA) is announcing 2026 award winners; the annual transit efficiency report honors top climate leaders and exposes urban carbon bottlenecks.
NEW YORK, NY — November 6, 2026


There are many things that we have gotten before the release of GTA VI like Bad Bunny at the Super Bowl, Taylor Swift's wedding, and finally Green Transit Alliance (GTA) releasing its annual public transit evaluation! 


To quote former Vice President Kamala Harris, "we didn't fall out a coconut tree," GTA deeply resonates with this. Thus, this evaluation report is a testament of its time, recognizing outstanding environmental efficiency among national transit providers while highlighting operational areas requiring urgent climate intervention. 


#### About the GTA Value Index (GTA VI)

The Green Transit Alliance Value Index (GTA VI) evaluates public transit agencies across the United States to measure their net environmental contribution. Rather than ranking agencies purely by size or passenger volume, the GTA VI measures operational efficiency by standardizing transit usage against comprehensive carbon accounting:

- Unlinked Passenger Trips (UPT): The total number of individual boardings across a transit system.

- Passenger Miles Traveled (PMT): The cumulative distance traveled by all passengers, accurately capturing long-distance commuter rail efficiency alongside dense city bus routes.

- Full-Lifecycle Emissions Accounting: Direct tailpipe emissions from diesel, gasoline, CNG, and bio-diesel fuels combined with indirect upstream power grid emissions generated by electrified rail and trolleybus networks (evaluated via state EIA grid carbon profiles).

By contrasting actual operational carbon footprints against a private passenger vehicle baseline, the GTA VI identifies transit agencies delivering maximum climate value per mile.


#### The Greenest Transit Agency (Overall)

Many are interested in knowing who won the Greenest Transit Agency award, but how do we measure it?

Well, the GTA VI evaluates the lbs of CO2 emitted per Passenger Mile Traveled (PMT) across high-capacity transit providers. PMT serves as the ultimate equalizer in transit analytics since it measures environmental cost per unit of actual passenger distance moved, preventing high-density metro rail systems and long-haul regional networks from being penalized for size.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 4.0


# Calculate dataset median (excluding NAs and zero values)
national_median_pmt <- median(normalized_emissions$emissions_per_pmt, na.rm = TRUE)

# Format the median for display (rounded to 3 decimals)
median_pmt_fmt <- round(national_median_pmt, 3)

# Dynamically calculate how many times more efficient WMATA is compared to the median
wmata_multiplier <- round(national_median_pmt / greenest_pmt, 0)

# 1. Pull the top 10 greenest agencies sorted from lowest to highest emissions
top10_greenest <- normalized_emissions %>%
  filter(!is.na(emissions_per_pmt), emissions_per_pmt > 0) %>%
  arrange(emissions_per_pmt) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(
    Agency_Short = str_trunc(`Agency Name`, 32),
    Is_Winner = if_else(`Agency Name` == greenest_name, "Winner", "Runner Up"),
    tooltip_text = glue("<b>{`Agency Name`}</b><br>Emissions: {round(emissions_per_pmt, 4)} lbs CO2/PMT")
  )

# 2. Build sorted bar chart (smallest emissions on the left)
p1 <- ggplot(top10_greenest, aes(x = reorder(Agency_Short, emissions_per_pmt), y = emissions_per_pmt, fill = Is_Winner)) +
  geom_col_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = tooltip_text, data_id = Agency_Short),
    width = 0.55,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(emissions_per_pmt, 3), " lbs")),
    vjust = -0.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.3,
    color = "#222222"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Winner" = "#BAFFC9", "Runner Up" = "#BAE1FF")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Greenest Transit Agencies in the US",
    subtitle = "Ranked by carbon efficiency (lbs CO2 per Passenger Mile Traveled)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "lbs CO2 / PMT",
    caption = "Source: FTA National Transit Database (NTD) & US EIA Energy Data"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 8.5, color = "#222222"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 20, l = 10),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 9)
  )

# Render interactive ggiraph plot
girafe(ggobj = p1, width_svg = 8.5, height_svg = 5.2)
```

Without further adieu, the top national honor for The Greenest Transit Agency goes to **`r greenest_name`**.

Taking advantage of heavy rail adoption and regional power grid efficiencies, `r greenest_name` achieved an extraordinary carbon rating of just **`r greenest_pmt` lbs of CO2 per passenger mile traveled**.

#### The Dishonorable NYC Carbon Guzzler Award

Zooming into NYC solely, we want to see what is happening in our backyard. 

The **NYC Carbon Guzzler Award** focuses specifically on transit providers in the New York metropolitan area, ranking them by **highest lbs of CO2 emitted per Passenger Mile Traveled (PMT)**. This metric isolates operations where low passenger occupancy, excessive route idling, or heavy reliance on direct fossil fuel combustion result in an inflated carbon footprint per mile moved.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false


library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggiraph)
library(gganimate)

# Step 1: Make 30 copies of the data, one per animation frame
guzzler_frames <- top_nyc_guzzlers |>
  mutate(agency_label = str_wrap(`Agency Name`, width = 25)) |>
  crossing(frame = 1:30) |>
  mutate(current_value = emissions_per_pmt * frame / 30)

# Step 2: Choose one pastel color per bar (add more colors if you show more than 5 agencies)
pastel_colors <- c("#FFB3BA",   # pastel red
                   "#FFDFBA",   # pastel orange
                   "#FFFFBA",   # pastel yellow
                   "#BAFFC9",   # pastel green
                   "#BAE1FF")   # pastel blue

# Step 3: Build the chart; fill = agency_label gives each bar its own color
guzzler_anim <- ggplot(guzzler_frames,
                       aes(x = current_value,
                           y = reorder(agency_label, emissions_per_pmt),
                           fill = agency_label)) +
  geom_col(color = "gray40") +                                    # thin outline so light bars stay visible
  geom_text(aes(label = round(current_value, 2)), hjust = -0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_colors) +                     # apply the pastel colors
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max(top_nyc_guzzlers$emissions_per_pmt) * 1.2),
                   breaks = seq(0, 3, by = 0.20)) +
  labs(title = "The NYC Carbon Guzzler Award",
       subtitle = "CO2 emissions per passenger mile traveled",
       x = "lbs of CO2 per passenger mile",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +                               # the agency names are already on the y-axis
  transition_manual(frame)

# Step 4: Render the GIF
animate(guzzler_anim, nframes = 30, fps = 10, end_pause = 15,
        width = 7, height = 4)
```

The dishonorable NYC Carbon Guzzler Award goes to *`r worst_nyc_agency`*, generating `r worst_nyc_pmt` lbs of CO2 per passenger mile traveled (totaling `r worst_nyc_co2` lbs of CO2 emissions).

#### Better Days Ahead

As public transit systems nationwide transition toward zero-emission fleet technology, the GTA VI framework highlights that operational choices from states and their policy truly dictates how green a public transit can be. Essentially, being more green should be more encouraged with incentives. High passenger occupancy and clean power grid integration remain the single most effective combination for decarbonizing urban mobility.

Although Grand Theft Auto VI is a much more popular household name, please do not confuse the Green Transit Alliance (GTA) with it. We are in a long-term legal battle to make them change their name, since we came first. We apologize for being the biggest cause of delay for Grand Theft Auto VI, but we are bleeding them of their money legally!
